preserved_initial_failures.disposition: Both original campaigns reached the 240-second deadline in the new fixture. Debugger captures show BSP in endpoint-node Box allocation waiting on the heap lock held by that same fixture; APs wait at the startup barrier. The fixture took a fresh storage capture after memory::budget::mark_platform, so trusted reserve admission correctly succeeded. This was a fixture classification error, not evidence of failed admission or insufficient limits.

Separately prove that a fresh capture after authorized promotion can use reserve outside the heap-held section, and close that temporary endpoint exactly. Add an aggregate original-node snapshot check around existing cancellation/staged-close controls. Production admission and numerical limits were unchanged by this correction.

Four preparation rejection stages restore exact node snapshot without authority serial/resource charge mutation. Existing cancellation, heap-held publication/detachment and staged close restore the original node snapshot before deliberate abandonment.

Existing preparation and close abandonment retain two nodes with lifecycle/mailbox/queue/table/kernel/physical/heap/account/global-node/endpoint-node guards held. No additional deliberately retained owner instance is introduced.

Existing real final-root recovery fixture retains two nodes/128 bytes through rejected invalidation, refunds before root backing on confirmed retry, preserves replacement on stale extraction, and retains original backing under actual guarded attempt abandonment.

Typed retired endpoint extracts mailbox resource charge outside shared node release; resource charge and backing charge both survive node deallocation. Explicit close, fixture cleanup and final-root release share this path. Shared retirement host controls verify deallocation-before-refund ordering.
